headline.text: OpenAI's Altman says the world should accept some bad things happening for AI's benefits

slides.altText: OpenAI's Altman says the world should accept some bad things happening for AI's benefits
slides.photoCredit: Steve Jurvetson, CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

slides.altText: Where Altman splits from Anthropic: "we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency." (Sam Altman)

quoteText.text: we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.

headline.text: He would turn down a no-hacks guarantee

slides.altText: He would turn down a no-hacks guarantee
slides.photoCredit: Village Global, CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

body.text: Altman said he would not take a trade guaranteeing no major hacks, no misuse and zero scams. He thinks people will do orders of magnitude more good than bad. The Verge notes he did not elaborate on the benefits.

headline.text: He still draws a line at catastrophe

slides.altText: He still draws a line at catastrophe

body.text: Altman said he does not accept the really catastrophic risks, including a serious loss of control to AI. Futurism calls that a walk-back and says where he draws the line is murky.
The Verge reports Altman said stronger regulation is still needed. He put OpenAI between Anthropic's more cautious approach and those favoring little or no regulation.

headline.text: The two labs had been moving closer

slides.altText: The two labs had been moving closer

body.text: Per Business Insider/Politico, OpenAI had backed stricter state safety laws and a House proposal for outside safety evaluators. Altman also agreed last month with Amodei's call to slow the most advanced models.

In an earlier Fortune interview, Altman said a 10% risk of AI killing everyone by the end of the decade is unacceptable. He also said alignment is not solved. Alignment is efforts to build AI aligned with human values.

slides.numberNote: Risk of AI killing everyone by end of decade that Altman called unacceptable (earlier Fortune interview)

headline.text: A cybersecurity CEO says Altman is wrong

slides.altText: A cybersecurity CEO says Altman is wrong

body.text: Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry said on Yahoo Finance that accepting the consequences is not acceptable, and that models and enterprises must each do their part. Zscaler sells protection against rogue AI agents, so it has a commercial interest.

caption:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said in Politico's new Decoded interview that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of AI, and he named that as a point where he differs from Anthropic and its CEO Dario Amodei.

Altman said he would not take a trade guaranteeing no major hacks, no misuse and zero scams, because he thinks people will do orders of magnitude more good than bad. He also said he does not accept the really catastrophic risks, including a serious loss of control to AI. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry said on Yahoo Finance that Altman is wrong. In an earlier Fortune interview, Altman called a 10% risk of AI killing everyone by the end of the decade unacceptable.
